FACT_ID: sec11-F01 | anchor: A01
Some revocations, suspensions, denials and cancellations can remain permanently recorded in a person’s driving history. [A01]
Why it matters: group License actions; recall cue License actions can remain on record.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec11-F02 | anchor: A01
Driving during suspension or revocation extends the withdrawal period and may result in imprisonment. [A01]
Why it matters: group License actions; recall cue Driving during withdrawal adds consequences.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec11-F03 | anchor: A01
Revocation withdraws driving privileges indefinitely; reapplication may become possible after at least one year unless a different rule applies. [A01]
Why it matters: group Revocation; recall cue Revocation is indefinite, reapplication is conditional.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec11-F04 | anchor: A01
A moving-violation conviction causing a fatal crash results in immediate license revocation. [A01]
Why it matters: group Revocation; recall cue Fatal moving-violation crash requires revocation.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec11-F05 | anchor: A01
The agency can revoke a repeat traffic offender’s license and may suspend vehicle registration during a revocation. [A01]
Why it matters: group Revocation; recall cue Repeated offenses can affect license and registration.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec11-F06 | anchor: A01
Aggravated impaired driving and driving under alcohol, cannabis or other drug impairment are among the listed revocation grounds. [A01]
Why it matters: group Revocation offenses; recall cue Impaired driving can cause revocation.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec11-F07 | anchor: A01
Aggravated flight from police, aggravated reckless driving and illegal drag or street racing are listed revocation grounds. [A01]
Why it matters: group Revocation offenses; recall cue Flight and dangerous racing threaten license.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec11-F08 | anchor: A01
Motor-vehicle or vehicle-parts theft and using a vehicle to commit a felony are listed grounds for revocation. [A01]
Why it matters: group Revocation offenses; recall cue Vehicle-related serious crime can revoke license.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec11-F09 | anchor: A01
Making, selling, possessing production equipment for or helping use an unauthorized nongovernmental identification card or license can lead to revocation. [A01]
Why it matters: group Revocation offenses; recall cue Unauthorized credential activity can revoke license.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec11-F10 | anchor: A02
Gang-related offenses involving a vehicle or Illinois license, false information to the agency and leaving an injury or fatal crash scene are listed revocation grounds. [A02]
Why it matters: group Revocation offenses; recall cue Misuse, false information and serious hit-and-run can revoke.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec11-F11 | anchor: A02
Reckless vehicle conduct causing injury or danger is a listed ground for revocation. [A02]
Why it matters: group Revocation offenses; recall cue Reckless conduct threatens privileges.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec11-F12 | anchor: A02
Three reckless-driving convictions in twelve months, or driving causing great bodily harm, permanent disability or disfigurement, are listed revocation grounds. [A02]
Why it matters: group Revocation offenses; recall cue Repeated or seriously injurious recklessness can revoke.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec11-F13 | anchor: A02
Reckless driving causing death, or a fatal crash while driving under an aggravated-impaired-driving suspension or revocation, is included in the reckless-homicide revocation listing. [A02]
Why it matters: group Revocation offenses; recall cue Fatal reckless conduct has revocation consequences.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec11-F14 | anchor: A02
A conviction for passing a school bus and causing a fatal crash is listed as a revocation ground. [A02]
Why it matters: group Revocation offenses; recall cue Fatal school-bus passing crash can revoke.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec11-F15 | anchor: A02
Suspension temporarily withdraws driving privileges; restoration after a fixed term requires the reinstatement fee and any other applicable conditions. [A02]
Why it matters: group Suspension; recall cue Suspension is temporary but restoration has conditions.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec11-F16 | anchor: A02
Five or more unpaid automated red-light or speeding violations in a municipality are listed as grounds for suspension. [A02]
Why it matters: group Suspension grounds; recall cue Repeated unpaid automated violations can suspend.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec11-F17 | anchor: A02
Failing to slow or change lanes in road work and causing damage or injury can lead to suspension. [A02]
Why it matters: group Suspension grounds; recall cue Work-zone crash conduct can suspend.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec11-F18 | anchor: A02
A court order finding violation of a child-visitation order can trigger suspension. [A02]
Why it matters: group Suspension grounds; recall cue Visitation order violation can affect license.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec11-F19 | anchor: A02
Refusing alcohol or drug chemical testing after an impaired-driving arrest in Illinois or another state is a listed suspension ground. [A02]
Why it matters: group Suspension grounds; recall cue Out-of-state test refusal can count.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec11-F20 | anchor: A02
Committing a drug or sex offense while operating or directly controlling a car is listed as a suspension ground. [A02]
Why it matters: group Suspension grounds; recall cue Certain offenses in vehicle control can suspend.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec11-F21 | anchor: A02
Failure to appear for a traffic citation before January first, two thousand twenty is a listed suspension ground. [A02]
Why it matters: group Suspension grounds; recall cue Historical failure-to-appear rule has date boundary.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec11-F22 | anchor: A02
A second conviction for ignoring a railroad-crossing signal is listed as a suspension ground. [A02]
Why it matters: group Suspension grounds; recall cue Repeat railroad-signal violation can suspend.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec11-F23 | anchor: A02
A child-support court order or direction from the responsible state department can suspend a license for nonpayment. [A02]
Why it matters: group Suspension grounds; recall cue Child-support enforcement can suspend license.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec11-F24 | anchor: A03
Failing to slow and move away from a stationary emergency vehicle and causing property damage or injury can lead to suspension. [A03]
Why it matters: group Suspension grounds; recall cue Responder-scene crash can affect license.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec11-F25 | anchor: A03
Using an altered or borrowed credential, lending a credential for misuse or submitting or facilitating a fraudulent application can lead to suspension. [A03]
Why it matters: group Suspension grounds; recall cue Credential fraud can suspend privileges.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec11-R01 | anchor: A01
Illegal alcohol possession, consumption, purchase or receipt by an under-twenty-one vehicle occupant is a listed suspension ground. [A01]
Why it matters: group Suspension grounds; recall cue Young occupant alcohol offense affects license.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec11-R02 | anchor: A01
For a person at least twenty-one, two illegal-alcohol-transportation offenses in twelve months can cause suspension; illegal transportation by someone younger than twenty-one is also listed. [A01]
Why it matters: group Suspension grounds; recall cue Alcohol transportation suspension varies by age.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec11-R03 | anchor: A01
Failure to file required financial-responsibility insurance after insurance-violation supervision or at least three uninsured-driving tickets can cause suspension. [A01]
Why it matters: group Suspension grounds; recall cue Required insurance filing must be maintained.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec11-R04 | anchor: A01
Driving without mandatory insurance and being an uninsured at-fault crash driver owing damages are listed suspension grounds. [A01]
Why it matters: group Suspension grounds; recall cue No insurance can lead to suspension.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec11-R05 | anchor: A01
Five or more unpaid railway-crossing violations are listed as a suspension ground. [A01]
Why it matters: group Suspension grounds; recall cue Unpaid railway violations can accumulate consequences.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec11-R06 | anchor: A01
Failing to stop for a school bus loading or unloading children, or leaving at least five camera-recorded stopped-bus yielding violations unpaid, can cause suspension. [A01]
Why it matters: group Suspension grounds; recall cue Stopped-bus duties have licensing consequences.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec11-R07 | anchor: A01
A second work-zone speeding violation within two years of the prior violation, when workers are present, is a listed suspension ground. [A01]
Why it matters: group Suspension grounds; recall cue Repeated worker-present work-zone speeding can suspend.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec11-R08 | anchor: A01
Refusing or neglecting to report a traffic crash is a listed suspension ground. [A01]
Why it matters: group Suspension grounds; recall cue Crash reporting protects license compliance.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec11-R09 | anchor: A01
The listed traffic-conviction suspension threshold is three within twelve months, or two within twenty-four months when the driver was younger than twenty-one at arrest. [A01]
Why it matters: group Suspension grounds; recall cue Young drivers have stricter conviction threshold.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec11-R10 | anchor: A01
Unauthorized parking in a disability-reserved space is a listed suspension ground. [A01]
Why it matters: group Suspension grounds; recall cue Accessible-space misuse can suspend privileges.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec11-R11 | anchor: A01
For someone younger than twenty-one, an alcohol concentration above zero but below zero point zero eight is listed as a zero-tolerance suspension ground. [A01]
Why it matters: group Suspension grounds; recall cue Young-driver zero tolerance reaches lower concentrations.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec11-R12 | anchor: A01
Cancellation formally ends a license or permit because of a defect, error or loss of entitlement; reapplication is allowed only after its conditions have been satisfied. [A01]
Why it matters: group Cancellation; recall cue Cancellation ends entitlement until conditions are met.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec11-R13 | anchor: A02
Missing or failing a required reexamination can lead to cancellation. [A02]
Why it matters: group Cancellation grounds; recall cue Required reexamination must be completed.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec11-R14 | anchor: A02
Fraud in a license or identification application and ineligibility for the credential are listed cancellation grounds. [A02]
Why it matters: group Cancellation grounds; recall cue Fraud or ineligibility can cancel credential.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec11-R15 | anchor: A02
Denial temporarily prevents applying for a license and sometimes a permit, and can be entered for specified convictions before age eighteen. [A02]
Why it matters: group Denial; recall cue Denial limits the ability to apply.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec11-R16 | anchor: A02
A minor’s conviction for a mandatory-revocation offense can prevent both license and permit applications until the eighteenth birthday. [A02]
Why it matters: group Denial; recall cue Minor revocation offense can deny both applications.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec11-R17 | anchor: A02
For a minor’s driving-without-valid-credential denial, a license cannot be requested until eighteen, but a permit remains available and an existing license is reduced to permit privileges. [A02]
Why it matters: group Denial; recall cue Minor unlicensed-driving denial preserves permit route.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec11-R18 | anchor: A02
A minor’s serious-moving-violation denial lasts nine months or until eighteen, whichever comes first, and restricts license applications while allowing a permit or reducing an existing license to permit privileges. [A02]
Why it matters: group Denial; recall cue Serious minor violation has shorter-of denial period.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec11-R19 | anchor: A02
A charge after a crash seriously injuring or killing another person may cause denial of license issuance or renewal even without alcohol involvement. [A02]
Why it matters: group Denial; recall cue Serious crash charge can prevent issuance.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec11-R20 | anchor: A02
A restricted permit limits driving to approved times and routes for listed work, education, child transport, medical care or substance-treatment purposes and cannot be issued below sixteen. [A02]
Why it matters: group Special permits; recall cue Restricted permit has purpose, route and age limits.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec11-R21 | anchor: A02
A monitoring permit may let an eligible first impaired-driving offender drive an interlock-equipped vehicle during summary suspension, provided the driver avoids alcohol before driving and does not tamper with the unit. [A02]
Why it matters: group Special permits; recall cue Monitoring relief depends on interlock compliance.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec11-R22 | anchor: A02
A monitoring-device permit cannot be issued to an applicant younger than eighteen. [A02]
Why it matters: group Special permits; recall cue Monitoring permit has minimum age.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec11-R23 | anchor: A03
An occupational permit can allow job-related driving after a professional driver’s three-moving-violation suspension, but it does not apply to commercial drivers. [A03]
Why it matters: group Special permits; recall cue Occupational permit excludes commercial drivers.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec11-R24 | anchor: A03
A probationary license may allow a driver at least twenty-one to drive during a suspension for three moving violations within twelve months in conjunction with driver-improvement participation. [A03]
Why it matters: group Special permits; recall cue Probationary relief requires stated age and program.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec11-R25 | anchor: A03
A family-financial-responsibility permit may allow driving after child-support or visitation-abuse suspension only following a circuit judge’s order or direction from the responsible state department. [A03]
Why it matters: group Special permits; recall cue Family-related permit requires official direction.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0065]
